transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. I'm a barber, and... well, I'm here because I've gotten to the point where I'll do almost anything to avoid using the straight razor at work. I'll switch clients with someone else, tell them the blade's missing, or just hide it in my drawer. And if I absolutely can't get out of it, I'm just shaking through the whole shave. It's become a real problem for me.
When you have to use the straight razor, are you afraid you might hurt the client with it?

Yeah, exactly. I mean... I know it’s just a tool, and it's what I trained with. I can use clippers all day long without any issue at all. But when that straight razor is just sitting open at my station, it really feels like I’m about to hurt somebody, or cut myself badly.
When you see or hold the straight razor, do unwanted thoughts or images pop into your mind of harming someone with it?

No, it's not really like that. I don't get, like, pictures in my head of doing something terrible on purpose or anything. It's just this intense fear that an accident is going to happen, that the blade is going to slip and someone is going to get hurt.
Outside of using the straight razor, do you find yourself worrying a lot about many other things in your life?

No, not really. I mean, I worry about normal stuff sometimes, like paying bills or if my car needs work, but it's nothing major. The only thing that really gets to me and makes me panic is that straight razor. Everything else is pretty much fine.
